goal: Locate the cause of intermittent payment timeouts spanning the API layer, service layer, and database access layer, and gather evidence for an implementation contract.

routing.basis: The investigation crosses distinct API, service, database, and log information boundaries; two independent bounded tasks can run concurrently.

economics.weighted_cost_rationale: Delegated source reading removes a larger context slice from the current Planner and uses the pre-authorized lower-cost task model; total tokens may increase and are not claimed as saved.

assumptions: Source descriptors refer to one consistent repository revision.
Token counts are estimates from the source index; they are not billing claims.
The Planner will show one dispatch notice before any in-policy PLAN task is started.

facts.statement: Timeouts occur between 5 and 8 seconds after payment submission.
The connection pool caps at 20 connections with a 30-second lease.

constraints: PLAN task Agents are read-only: no product-code writes, no requirement changes, no user interaction, no contract authoring, and no spawned Agents.
Every material claim must cite a precise source locator.

sources.purpose: Shared request/response types and error codes used across all layers
sources.summary: Small common interface needed by API and service tasks.

sources.purpose: Payment submission endpoint, timeout configuration, retry behavior
Payment orchestration, transaction boundaries, downstream calls
Connection pooling, lease handling, timeout propagation
Timestamped timeout traces correlating requests across layers

tasks.objective: Determine how the payment endpoint configures timeouts and retries and what the logs show about where the 5-8 second window originates.
questions: What is the configured client-facing timeout and does it match the 5-8 second window?
Do the logs show timeouts originating at the API layer or passed up from below?
Is there a retry that doubles perceived latency?
tasks.deliverable: Findings on API-layer timeout behavior with exact locators and log line references.
stop_conditions: All listed questions are answered or explicitly blocked.

tasks.objective: Determine how the payment service manages transaction boundaries and downstream calls during the timeout window.
questions: Which downstream calls sit on the critical path of payment submission?
Are transaction boundaries held across slow calls?
Is there any lock or serialization point on the payment path?
tasks.deliverable: Findings on service-layer call structure with exact locators.
stop_conditions: All critical-path calls and their failure modes are accounted for.

tasks.objective: Determine whether connection-pool lease behavior explains intermittent timeouts.
questions: Can pool exhaustion delay connection acquisition past the client timeout?
Are leases released on all failure paths?
Does the pool timeout propagate as a retryable error?
tasks.deliverable: Findings on pool behavior under load with exact locators.
stop_conditions: All lease acquisition and release paths in scope are accounted for.

final_checks: Every accepted material finding has a source locator.
The root-cause hypothesis is consistent with the log timeline.
No conclusion depends on mismatched source versions.
The Planner records context savings, delegated input, result size, and weighted-cost rationale without claiming total-token savings.
